title: fix(post): a touch probe section starts no spindle on any mill post
body:
## What changed

A touch probe is never spun (#523). Haas, Tormach, Sinumerik, Heidenhain and Mazak posted `S<rpm> M3` (Mazak `MOTON S…`) for every section, a probe's S0 included. Each now gates its spindle start on `sRpm > 0`, the rule `fanuc.cps` has used since #108. Heidenhain also drops the `S` word from its `TOOL CALL` at rpm 0.

- No extra `M5` is needed: every post already ends each section with `M5`, so a probe section never inherits a running spindle.
- A cutter can never lose its spindle through this: `Tool::is_sane` refuses rpm 0 on every tool, so S0 reaches a post only from a probe dump.
- **Reachability:** on main, only Fanuc posts probe moves, and it was already gated. PR #500 (Tormach probe positioning) makes the Tormach path reachable, which is where `S0 M3` showed up in the Hub run. #500 should merge after this.

## How tested

New suite `crates/app/tests/probe_spindle.rs`:
- `a_section_with_no_spindle_speed_starts_no_spindle_on_any_mill_post`: an rpm-0 section through all six mill posts posts no `S` word and no `M3`/`M03`/`MOTON`. It fails without the post changes (`haas: a probe section posts ["S0", "M3"]`).
- `a_cutting_section_still_starts_its_spindle_on_every_mill_post`: an 8000 rpm section still posts its `S` word and spindle start on all six.

`scripts/gate.sh quick`, which escalated to batch, ran 782 s. Results:
- geometry, cl, tools, post, sim and motion: green.
- app: green, 1433 passed and 0 failed across all binaries, conformance and every NC golden byte-exact.
- clippy `-D warnings` on all 8 crates: green.
- ui: the only red is the five known failures that are also red on main: the three headless tests that need a GPU adapter, and `structural::shell_structure_dark/light` (the `v0.0.0` label).

## Not exercised

No Hub run. No posted program on main reaches the changed path except through Fanuc, which is unchanged. Cutting output is byte-identical, since every golden is unchanged.

Changelog: A probing section no longer starts the spindle (S0 M3) on the Haas, Tormach, Siemens, Heidenhain and Mazak posts (#523)

Fixes #523

title: fix(ui): browser tree rows read on the light panel
body:
## What changed

The browser tree's rows were pale grey on the light panel (#506).

- **Root cause:** egui keeps a dark and a light style and follows the OS appearance. `theme::apply_to` wrote the token table only into the slot that was active at startup. On a Mac in light mode, egui switched to its stock light visuals while the painted tree kept drawing our table's ink on that panel. `apply_to` now writes the table into **both** slots, so the document's theme is the only theme.
- **Row ink:** tree rows no longer use `text_faint`, the disabled tier, which reads about 3:1 on the light strip. A hidden row and the suffix use `text_dim`. A selected row is all `text`, because `text_dim` reads only 3.5:1 on the dark theme's selection fill. The rule lives in `painted::row_inks`.

## How it was tested

- New `egui_app::tree_ink_tests` (lib):
  - `tree_row_ink_clears_body_contrast_on_every_row_ground`: every row ink clears WCAG body contrast (4.5:1) on every ground it is painted on (panel, strip, hover, selection), in both built-in themes.
  - `applied_theme_fills_both_egui_theme_slots`: both egui slots carry the applied table, and flipping the OS theme keeps the table's panel fill.
- `scripts/gate.sh quick`, which escalated to batch, ran 9 steps. Green: geometry, cl, tools, post, sim, motion, app, ui integration suites, clippy `-D warnings` on all 8 crates.
- Red in the `camcraft-ui` lib and binaries, all unrelated to this change:
  - three headless tests that need a GPU adapter the gate machine did not provide: `headless_run_succeeds`, `egui_headless_cli_exit_code_is_zero`, `headless_cli_exit_code_is_zero`;
  - `structural::shell_structure_dark/light` (`"v0.0.0"` version label). These are confirmed red on current main too.

## Not exercised

The look on a real screen, which needs a hands-on check in light and dark mode. That is why this PR stays a draft.

Changelog: The browser tree's rows read clearly on the light theme; the theme no longer follows the OS appearance behind the user's back (#506)

Fixes #506

title: fix(app): a typed Slot's caps no longer read as a gouge
body:
## What changed

A typed Slot whose cutter reaches its round caps was reported as a Gouge on every plunge and feed, so it never posted (#510). The cause was the region the verifier checks a Slot against, `operation::material::stadium`. It drew each cap as 16 chords **inscribed** in the true arc. A chord sits up to `h(1 - cos 5.625°)` inside the arc, and the slot generator's passes follow the true arc exactly, so the gouge check (`d(centre, boundary) >= r - GOUGE_TOL`) flagged a cutter that only touched the cap.

The caps are now the polygon **circumscribed** about the arc. Every chord is tangent to the arc, and the corners sit at `h / cos(phi/2)`. The chord count is set per slot (`cap_segments`) so a corner stands at most `CAP_SAG_BUDGET = 0.001 mm` outside the arc, with 16 to 2048 chords per cap. The first and last corner of each cap lie on the lines of the straight sides, so the sides stay exact. `GOUGE_TOL` is unchanged.

**Posted G-code: unchanged.** The generator is untouched. Only the gouge verdict changes, plus the drawn region outline, which moves by at most 1 µm.

## Readings (80×60×20 stock, EM-0600-4FL, a=(-15,0), b=(15,0), Top 20, Bottom 10, stepdown 5)

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| width 6 (centreline pass) | `Gouge` at moves 2, 3, 7, 8, 12, 13; post blocked | no warnings; posts |
| width 10 (rings at ±2) | `Gouge` on all 18 plunges/feeds; post blocked | no warnings; posts |
| cap-centre distance to boundary (r = 3) | 2.9855 (needs ≥ 2.99) | ≥ 3.0 (tangent) |
| path pushed +0.05 mm in X past the cap | (already convicted) | still convicted |

## Top-Z pass

The issue also reports that a Slot makes a feed pass at its Top before stepping down. The other 2D ladders do the same: `cut_levels(top, bottom, step)` starts at Top for pocket, contour, circular, trace, face and the 3D entries. It is an air pass, never a gouge. This PR pins the current behaviour rather than changing one op on its own. The decision file explains why and recommends a separate issue if the first level should be `top - stepdown` for every ladder.

## Tests

New `crates/app/tests/slot_caps.rs`:
- `a_slot_riding_its_round_caps_verifies_clean_and_posts`: widths 6 and 10, each run with stock as the source and with a slotted part model as the source. Each run has no Gouge, no warning that blocks posting, and `post_setup` writes the program.
- `a_slot_driven_past_its_cap_is_still_a_gouge`: the generated path, shifted 0.05 mm past the cap and checked against the op's own `region_of`, is convicted. The unshifted path checks clean.
- `the_stadium_region_hugs_the_true_caps`: at 721 angles on both caps, the true arc is inside the region and a point 2 µm past it is outside.
- `the_slot_ladder_starts_at_the_authored_top`: the cut levels are [20, 15, 10].

Before the fix, the first three fail and the fourth passes.

Gate (debug): camcraft-app lib (101), slot_caps, operations, area_controls, cutting_data, project_roundtrip, golden_cl, verify and blind_floor all pass. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised

- The release `--ignored` lanes. No goldens move, because the generator output is unchanged.
- The UI region-outline drawing (the outline moves by at most 1 µm).
- Hand-run in the GUI or on a real machine.

Decision file: `docs/decisions/510-slot-cap-region.md`.

Changelog: A typed Slot whose cutter reaches its round ends is no longer falsely reported as a gouge, so it posts again (#510)

Fixes #510

title: fix(sim): judge spindle-C moves at the station pose and fixed steel in the machine frame
body:
Fixes a missed fixture hit under a spindle-C turn (#486). Two causes, both reproduced on main first.

## What was wrong
1. **Fixed steel was judged in the part frame only.** For a C move the live tool never leaves its station (+X), so steel there is hit at every C. The part-frame reading only saw it near C 0; `posed_steel::upright_turn` answers Unjudged for that pose, so the part-frame verdict stood. End to end: a Rotary Contour on the mill-turn C bar with a fixed steady at the station had no hit on the far side of the bar (C≈180), and the post gate was silent too.
2. **Steel riding the part was judged at the wrong pose.** `cl::stamp_c` gave every piece of a split move the move's end axis, while mid-turn the tool points along the diagonal. A chuck jaw on the diagonal at holder radius was silent.

## What changed
- `crates/cl/src/cl/rotary.rs`: `split` stamps each piece with the station pose at its own C (the move's axis turned by the turn left in the move). The last piece keeps the move's axis bit for bit. The post writes only C for C moves, so the stream and the `c_axis_helix.nc` golden are unchanged.
- New `crates/sim/src/verify/c_steel.rs`:
  - `station_poses` reads each C move's pose from its C, so toolpaths cached before this fix are judged right at the gate without regenerating.
  - `fixed_hits` judges fixed steel in the machine frame along the station ray.
  - The spindle line is recovered from the stamped tips, then from the op's rotary axis, and used only if every tip sits on its ray within 1e-4 mm. With no line, or an arc or non-finite C move, a C move against fixed steel is a hit (fails closed).
- `crates/sim/src/verify/workholding.rs`: both `_held` wrappers judge the station-posed path, then add the machine-frame fixed-steel hits. Add-only: no existing verdict loosens.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/486-stamp-c-axis.md`.

## How tested
- sim `c_axis_fixture` (8). Fail on main: `the_machine_meets_fixed_steel_at_the_station_mid_turn` (line given and line unknown), `a_rapid_turn_past_fixed_steel_convicts_as_a_rapid`, `steel_riding_the_part_meets_the_pose_the_turn_passes_through`, `every_stamped_piece_states_the_station_pose_at_its_own_c`. Also `a_path_stamped_before_486_is_read_at_the_pose_its_c_states`, plus clear and fail-closed controls.
- app `c_axis_fixture` (2): `fixed_steel_at_the_station_convicts_cuts_on_the_far_side_of_the_bar` (fails on main; checks generation and `posting::fixture_findings`) and an off-station control.
- Unit tests in `cl::rotary` and `verify::c_steel`.
- Quick gate (escalated to batch because `cl` changed): every suite green except the known headless-GPU ui tests (no adapter on this Mac). After merging main (#491's `arc_bulge`, a `mod` line conflict): sim `c_axis_fixture`, `posed_fixture`, `fixture_stack_span`, app `c_axis_fixture`, `fixtures` and `c_axis_live` pass; clippy `-D warnings` is clean on cl, sim and app.
- Verdicts in existing suites are unchanged; the only new verdicts are the newly caught hits.

## Not exercised
No posted G-code changes (C-only output and goldens unchanged), so no machine run is needed. May touch the same `verify/mod.rs` area as #488 (a `mod` line at most).

Changelog: Fixture checks under a spindle-C turn judge the tool at its machine station pose: fixed steel at the live-tool station and part-riding steel mid-turn are now caught instead of passing the post gate (#486)

Fixes #486

title: fix(post): the Siemens 840D safe retract comes from the machine file
body:
Stacked on #501 (which is stacked on #477) — merge those first. Until then this PR's diff against `main` also shows their commits; this PR's own change is commit acbc6b6c.

## What changed

`sinumerik.cps` lifted Z with `G53 Z0` in two places: the after-operation home move and the program end. That assumes machine Z0 is the top of Z travel. Siemens' public documentation leaves the reference point and machine zero to the machine builder, so the post now reads #495's `machine.safeRetractZ`, the same way #501 does for the Tormach post:

- **Stated value** (0 included) posts `G0 G53 Z<v>` + `G0 G53 X0 Y0` for a home move, and `G53 Z<v>` at the end. The value is in mm, which is the unit this dialect writes. A non-zero value also adds the header comment `; SAFE RETRACT G53 Z<v> - STATED BY THE MACHINE`.
- **No machine** (null or unnamed) keeps today's `G53 Z0`, byte-identical.
- **A named machine that states no value** gets one counted `message()` naming the machine and the `safe_retract` key, and no retract is written. The XY half of the home move is dropped too, so XY never moves without the Z lift first. The in-app gate blocks the write.
- **No name exemption.** #501 exempts Tormach because PathPilot defines the top-of-travel convention. Siemens documents no such rule, so a model named "Siemens …" is refused like any other.

Docs: `assets/posts/AGENTS.md`, `assets/machines/AGENTS.md`, and the decision file `docs/decisions/503-sinumerik-safe-retract.md`.

**Output change:** none for anything shipped. Every shipped mill file and the default `3axis-vmc.mch` (the conformance goldens' machine) state 0, and the goldens are byte-exact. A user machine without the key, `millturn.mch`, or a document saved before #495 with a mounted machine is now refused by name through this post.

## How tested

New suite `crates/app/tests/sinumerik_safe_retract.rs`:
- `a_stated_z0_and_no_machine_post_byte_identical`: null machine and default VMC keep `G53 Z0`. Every shipped Z0 machine posts the same program as the no-machine path, apart from the name line.
- `a_stated_safe_z_posts_that_z`: covers both the mirror and the raw-file door. Z290 is posted at the home move and at the end, with the header comment. An inch file's 11.5 is posted as Z292.1.
- `a_machine_without_a_safe_z_is_refused_by_name`: covers both doors, and a "Siemens"-named model as well. The machine is refused once and no G53 is written.

Two fixture updates: `coolant.rs` and `coolant_followups.rs` built a bare `Machine` that they post through every mill post. They now state `safe_retract_z: Some(0.0)`.

Gate:
- `cargo test -p camcraft-post`: all green.
- Every `camcraft-app` debug test binary (172) is green, including conformance (goldens byte-exact), tormach_safe_retract, after_op, posting, coolant, and program_comments. The only one not run is the slow `center_cut_multiaxis` lane, which does not post.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --tests -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised

- No real machine and no Hub sim.
- The `G75` fixed-point form (Siemens' documented tool-change position move) was considered and not adopted. See the decision file.
- The UI machine sheet still does not show the key (same as #501).

Changelog: Siemens 840D post retracts to the machine's stated safe Z (`safe_retract`, machine coordinates) and refuses a machine that states none, instead of assuming machine Z0 is the top of travel

Fixes #503

title: fix(post): the Tormach safe retract comes from the machine file
body:
## What changed

The Tormach post's safe retract `G53 G0 Z0` assumed machine Z0 is the top of Z travel. That holds on a Tormach, but on a LinuxCNC machine homed with Z0 at the bottom it rapids down into the part (reported on #435).

- **Machine file:** an optional `safe_retract` on the linear Z part gives the retract Z in MACHINE coordinates, in the file's length unit (scaled like travel). Zero counts as a stated value. A non-number, or the key on any other axis, refuses the file and names the axis. The mirror carries it as `safeRetractZ` (mm). The script sees `machine.safeRetractZ` (or `null`) and `machine.model`, the model name through either door (app mirror or CLI raw file).
- **Shipped machines:** every Tormach `.mch` states `0.0`. So do `vmc.mch`, `tilthead.mch` and the default `3axis-vmc.mch` (`"safeRetractZ": 0.0`).
- **tormach.cps:**
  - A stated safe Z posts `G53 G0 Z<that>`.
  - With no machine, or a model named "Tormach..." that states no safe Z, the output is unchanged (`G53 G0 Z0` + `G30`).
  - Any other machine that states no safe Z gets one counted `message()` that names the machine and the key, and no retract line is written. The in-app gate blocks the write.
  - A non-zero safe Z drops `G30`, because an unset G30 position on LinuxCNC is the machine origin. The header then says `(SAFE RETRACT G53 Z<v> - STATED BY THE MACHINE)`.
- **Docs:** `assets/machines/AGENTS.md`, `assets/posts/AGENTS.md`, `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md`, and the decision file `docs/decisions/495-safe-retract.md` (alternatives considered, plus notes on the other posts).

## How tested

New `crates/app/tests/tormach_safe_retract.rs`:
- `the_shipped_tormach_machines_post_byte_identical`: every library Tormach posts byte-identical with and without the key. A null machine and the default VMC also keep `G53 G0 Z0` / `G30`.
- `a_stated_safe_z_posts_that_z`: covers the mirror and the raw door. An inch file scales, there is no G30, and the header comment is written.
- `a_non_tormach_machine_without_a_safe_z_is_refused_by_name`: covers the mirror and the raw door, and checks that a Tormach-named file without the key still posts Z0.
- `a_garbled_safe_retract_refuses_the_file`

Gate: `cargo test -p camcraft-post` (all), plus 64 camcraft-app suites touching posts and machines, all green. These include conformance (every golden byte-exact), tormach_post, tormach_machines, machine, machine_library, posting, fanuc_post, inverted_post, program_comments, project_roundtrip, wear_comp and control_comp. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --tests -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised

- No real machine cut and no Hub sim.
- The UI machine sheet does not show the new key yet.
- The CLI `post` binary was not smoke-run by hand. Its raw-door path is covered by the tests.
- Behaviour change: a document saved before this change with a mounted non-Tormach machine (for example the library "VMC 3-axis") stores that machine without the key. Posting it through the Tormach post is now refused by name until the machine is re-mounted.

Changelog: Tormach post retracts to the machine's stated safe Z (`safe_retract`, machine coordinates) and refuses a non-Tormach machine that states none, instead of assuming machine Z0 is the top of travel

Fixes #495

title: test(sim): pin that the fixture box laws already convict every mesh penetration
body:
**Stacked on #476** (#339 slice 1, fixture mesh). Slice 2 of #339, answered by tests rather than new law. The full analysis is posted on #339.

## What this is
Slice 2 asked whether the mesh law must also **convict**: catch penetrations the box laws let through.

**Answer: no.**
- A meshed fixture's box is the exact AABB of the same transformed vertices the mesh law reads (`model::entity_world_aabb` / `world_facets`). `mesh_refined` only reads a mesh whose AABB equals the law's box, and non-finite meshes keep the box verdict. So the mesh always sits inside its box, rotated fixtures and overhangs included.
- Every deliberate silence of the box laws allows an overlap of at most `FIXTURE_HIT_TOL` (1e-9) with the box. That covers the strict z overlap in `band_hits_box` (c2, plus #464's d2 upper bands and flute column) and the strict-dip rule in `rapid_hits_box`. An overlap that small with the box can't be more than that with the mesh.
- Everything else is an enclosure, not a silence.

## What changed
New `crates/sim/tests/fixture_mesh_convict.rs` (5 tests, with a gate-map header). Each composes the box laws with `mesh_refined` the way `posting::fixture_problems` does.
- **A mesh top face keeps the strict dip:** a retract off it, a traverse riding it and a cut riding it are silent. The same moves 0.001 lower report Rapid and Flute.
- **A rotated fixture's top edge is its box's top:** a block turned 45° about X, then 30° about Z.
- **An overhanging arm convicts the stack under it:** the Shank under the arm and the Holder rim off its end both hit. Its top stays flush-silent.
- **The #424 and #425 repros convict on a closed mesh** (Holder), from the box law and the mesh alike.
- **No straight move the box laws clear penetrates the mesh:** a seeded sweep of 12,000 moves biased onto flush planes. 7,045 are silent (103 in flush contact), and none penetrates the mesh. Lowering the box top 0.01 mm makes this test fail at once, which shows it catches real gaps.

## Found along the way (filed separately)
**#491:** the box laws judge an XY arc by its **inscribed** chords at the bare band radius, so steel within the arc's sagitta (about 0.01 mm on R30) is missed. This applies to every fixture, not only meshed ones, so the fix belongs in the box law. It is out of this slice's scope.

## How tested
- `fixture_mesh_convict` 5/5, `fixture_mesh` 9 passed (1 ignored), `fixture_stack_span` 8/8.
- `clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --tests -D warnings` is clean.
- Test-only: no product code changes.

Changelog: none (test-only)

Refs #339

title: feat(sim): judge posed, rotary and XZ/YZ-arc moves against the fixture mesh
body:
**Stacked on #476** (#339 slice 1, fixture mesh). Slice 3 of #339 per the triage on the issue: posed, rotary and XZ/YZ-arc moves read against the fixture mesh. Slice 1 left those on the box verdict. As before, **the mesh only ever clears a hit the box law flagged; it never adds one.**

## What changed
**Frames.**
- **Path frame:** steel that turns with the part, and any steel when no rotary axis is stated (the box laws' frame).
- **Machine frame, A rotary:** fixed steel under an A rotary op, carried per stretch by `posed_steel::upright_turn`, the same frame `workholding` uses. A pose the rotary alone can't stand upright keeps the box verdict.
- **Machine frame, spindle C:** each move's C line is recovered from its two stated C angles. Fixed steel gets one exact sweep of the machine's straight station run. Steel turning with the part is read along the real spiral, in stretches turned by −C.
- **XZ/YZ arcs:** chorded in their own plane, with the same sagitta pad as XY arcs.
- **Left to the box:**
  - a C move whose start C isn't the previous move's;
  - a non-horizontal C pose;
  - a C turn under 1e-4 rad or near 180°;
  - a held C under fixed steel;
  - fixed steel under both a rotary axis and C;
  - an arc on a C move.

**Why a "clear" is safe.**
1. Each posed move is split into stretches by its pose turn (`midpose::turn_intervals`). Over a stretch the tip stays on its segment within the chord pad, and the pose stays within `swing` of the stretch axis, by midpose's existing rate bound.
2. A band point `p(t) + Q(t)y` stays within `swing·hypot(max(|lo|,|hi|), r)` of the unturned band. So the band lies inside segment ⊕ oriented cylinder ⊕ ball(pad), a convex set.
3. GJK sweeps the segment and cylinder exactly, and the ball goes into the margin. "Clear" is returned only with a separating-plane proof. A non-finite input or NaN margin counts as a hit.
4. A turn into another frame adds `dth·ρmax`, with ρmax taken at the stretch's four parallelogram corners plus r + pad. Distance to a line is convex, so that bounds it.
5. Consecutive stretches overlap at their shared instant, so one inside-the-solid point per band decides. Using an oriented cylinder rather than a capsule means a tilted tool isn't falsely convicted on a vise floor below its tip.

**Labels.** A mesh-kept rapid hit names a band above the flute by its part (Shank, Holder, Spindle), like #464's law (d2). This now applies on the posed and C paths too.

`docs/decisions/339-mesh-posed.md`, including a finding filed as **#486**: `cl::stamp_c` pieces keep the whole move's tool axis, so the box laws may misjudge fixed steel on C turns. The mesh can't fix that, since it only clears hits.

## How tested
- **New sim `fixture_mesh_posed`** (9 tests, plus 1 heavy-lane):
  - a tilted pass, an in-place index and a tilted rapid down a vise gap are cleared, while the same index into a jaw and a rapid swung into the other jaw still convict;
  - A-rotary fixed and turning steel, each with a clear case and a convicting case;
  - C turns with turning and fixed steel; a move with no prior C, and an axial tool, keep the box verdict;
  - XZ arcs, one clear and one dipping 0.21 mm into the base; a YZ arc in the gap is clear;
  - a posed rapid kept by the mesh names its band;
  - both turn signs (A and C) pinned by mutation.
- **New app `fixture_mesh_posed`** (2 tests): a 3+2 face indexed B 10° between closed jaws. The box law alone convicts every move, yet the post and generation are clean. With the jaws 1 mm into reach, the post is blocked and generation warns.
- **One slice-1 pin renamed** (`unpaired_boxes_keep_the_box_verdict_and_posed_moves_are_read`): a posed gap pass is now cleared.
- **Existing suites keep their verdicts:** posed_fixture, posed_fixture_midpose, posed_rapids, midmove_pose, fixture_stack_span, sim lib; app fixtures, rotary_fixtures, fixture_mesh, fixture_law_gaps. Their fixtures are box-only or open, so the mesh never judges them.
- **Performance:**
  - debug, 29.7k facets and 80 posed moves: 0.07 s;
  - release heavy lane, 203k facets and 2000 posed moves: 0.33 s.
- `clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --tests -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised
No GUI or G-code change. More 4/5-axis and rotary programs now post: those whose only "hit" was a box around empty space between jaws.

Changelog: Fixture collisions on tilted, rotary and spindle-C moves and XZ/YZ arcs are judged against the fixture's real mesh too, so a tilted pass between vise jaws no longer refuses the post (#339)

title: feat(ui): fixture UX - mark/import from the browser, mesh state, struck tint
body:
**Stacked on #476** (#339 slice 1, fixture mesh). Slice 4 of #339 per the triage on the issue: fixture UX.

## What changed
1. **Browser.**
   - A model row's context menu (under Models or a setup's Fixtures) offers **Use as fixture (<active setup>)** and **Stop using as fixture**. They reuse the existing `TagFixture` / `UntagFixture` commands, so undo and redo work.
   - A setup's Fixtures node offers **Import fixture…**, which reuses the existing dialog and activates that setup.
2. **Mesh state per fixture.**
   - Each Fixtures row ends in `mesh`, or `box only: <reason>`: open mesh, non-finite, collapsed, over the facet cap, no facets, or shared box. The reasons come from #476's `FixtureMesh::build`.
   - A mesh refusal is reported ahead of a shared box, since the user can fix it.
   - The Fixtures page shows the full sentence as a `Collision:` label.
   - The app helper is `fixture_view::mesh_states`, cached per document version.
3. **Highlight.** `FixtureHit` names the op, move and band, but not the fixture.
   - For the selected op, `fixture_struck::struck_by` re-runs the gate's own law against each fixture alone and keeps the ones that reproduce a warned move.
   - Those fixtures are tinted in the gouge colour, and the op banner names them ("Strikes fixture: …").
   - A warned move no fixture reproduces (e.g. a jaw moved without regenerating) says "Fixture not resolved for move N … regenerate to re-check" and tints nothing, rather than guessing.
   - Display only, cached per document version, op and path.

**Behaviour changes to note:**
- **Import as fixture is now one undo unit.** The new `ImportFixture` command applies and inverts the import, or the update of an existing name, together with the fixture marker. `crates/ui/tests/fixtures.rs::import_as_fixture_lands_as_two_undo_units` became `…_one_undo_unit`; the test count is unchanged.
- **A refused import now clears the pending fixture binding**, so it can't tag the next, unrelated import.
- **`posting::fixture_problems`'s per-op workholding check now calls `fixture_struck::op_hits`**, the same function the highlight uses, so the gate and the viewport can't disagree. Same logic, and app suites green.

`docs/decisions/339-fixture-ux.md`

## How tested
- App `fixture_ux` (8 tests):
  - closed, open and NaN mesh states, the shared box, and the version cache;
  - mark and unmark with undo;
  - `ImportFixture` fresh and as an update, with undo, redo and refusals;
  - the struck jaw is named and the clear one isn't;
  - a moved jaw is reported unresolved, not guessed;
  - no warnings resolves to nothing.
- UI `egui_app::fixture_ux_tests` (6 tests):
  - the menu rows and their commands, through the queue and undo;
  - the row suffixes;
  - the tint flag (exactly one part carries `STRUCK_CLASS`) and the banner line;
  - the unresolved banner;
  - the Fixtures page's refusal text.
- **No snapshot PNG touched.**
- App suites green. In ui, only the three headless-GPU tests fail (no adapter on this Mac), as on main. `clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --tests -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised (draft until the contributor's GUI check)
A hands-on check. A test kit is prepared: a project with a struck jaw, a clear jaw, an open-mesh jaw, and a plain model to mark.

Changelog: Fixtures: mark or import a fixture from the browser, see whether each fixture is judged by its mesh or only its box (and why), and see which fixture a warned move strikes (#339)

Refs #339
